mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (<=0.5%) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations and reduces discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer spending (RSAFS) growth exceeds 0.5% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is above 3.0% annually, the market anticipates aggressive monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL annual growth > 3.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when RSAFS growth > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL annual growth > 3.0% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market with low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong job growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.3% MoM), the S&P 500 produces positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to sustained economic expansion and corporate earnings growth.
regime_hint: low unemployment and strong job growth
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.3% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) are associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as increased residential construction activity signals robust economic growth and rising consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST > median(HOUST) (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates robust economic activity and strong corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO growth > 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL annual growth > 3.0%) is high and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 600, the market anticipates aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and strong housing market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when CPIAUCSL annual growth > 3.0% and HOUST > 600 (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% quarter-over-quarter), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 20 trading days due to sustained corporate earnings and investor confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when GDPC1 growth > 2.0% QoQ (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero mean).
